title: Direct Connect & Site-to-Site VPN
summary: Private, consistent links to on-premises networks and how to make them resilient and encrypted.
tldr: **Site-to-Site VPN**: encrypted IPsec over the internet, up in minutes, cheap, variable latency. **Direct Connect**: a private physical link with consistent performance and lower data transfer out rates, but it takes weeks to provision and **isn't encrypted by default**.
Encrypt DX with **MACsec** (10, 100 or 400 Gbps dedicated ports, not hosted connections) or a **VPN over DX**. Make it resilient with a second DX at another location, or a VPN as backup.

Reach VPCs in many Regions from one DX with a **Direct Connect gateway**. Reach many VPCs at scale with a **transit VIF to a transit gateway**. Connect your own sites over the AWS backbone with **SiteLink**.

keyFacts.text: Maximum bandwidth of a standard VPN tunnel (newer large bandwidth tunnels reach 5 Gbps). Aggregate more with **ECMP** across BGP (dynamic) VPNs on a transit gateway.
Dedicated DX port speeds. **Hosted connections** from a partner range from 50 Mbps to 25 Gbps, so you can right-size a mostly idle link.
**Private VIF** to a VGW or DX gateway, **public VIF** to AWS public endpoints, **transit VIF** to transit gateways through a DX gateway.
A **Direct Connect gateway** is a global object: one private or transit VIF can reach VPCs in many Regions without extra circuits.
Each Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels to separate AWS endpoints for redundancy. Configure both on the customer gateway, or maintenance on one tunnel drops the link.

traps: Direct Connect is **not encrypted** by default; "DX is AES-256 encrypted" is false.
DX takes weeks to provision, so it fails any "within a week" requirement.
A virtual private gateway doesn't support ECMP across VPN connections; you need a transit gateway.
Private VIFs attach to one VGW in one Region; for several Regions use a DX gateway, not one VIF per VPC.
S3 gateway endpoints can't be used from on premises; on-premises access needs an interface endpoint.
A link aggregation group (LAG) adds bandwidth at one location; it doesn't save money on an underused link (downsize to a hosted connection) and isn't location-level resilience.
Accelerated VPN and ECMP both need a transit gateway; neither works on a VPN that ends on a virtual private gateway.
